title: Go: Recursion
description: Write recursive functions — factorial, fibonacci, tail recursion, and memoization.

steps.title: Basic Recursion — Factorial
steps.description: Write a recursive function `factorial(n int) int` that returns `n!` and print `factorial(5)`.

verification.failureMessage: Compute factorial(5)=120 using recursion and print it.

steps.title: Multiple Recursive Calls — Fibonacci
steps.description: Write a recursive function `fib(n int) int` for fibonacci and print `fib(7)`.

verification.failureMessage: Compute fib(7)=13 using recursion and print it.

steps.title: Tail Recursion
steps.description: Write a tail-recursive function `factTail(n, acc int) int` for factorial and call it with `factTail(5, 1)`.
hints: Tail recursion passes the accumulated result as a parameter.

verification.failureMessage: Compute 5! using tail recursion with accumulator and print 120.

steps.title: Recursive Data Structure
steps.description: Define a `Tree` struct with `Value int` and `Left, Right *Tree`. Write a function `sum(t *Tree) int` that sums all values. Create a small tree and print the sum.
hints: `type Tree struct { Value int; Left, Right *Tree }`

verification.failureMessage: Create a tree {1, {2, nil, nil}, {3, {4, nil, nil}, nil}} and print sum 10.

steps.title: Memoization
steps.description: Write a memoized version of fibonacci using a map `memo map[int]int` passed as a parameter. Print `fibMemo(10, memo)`.
hints: `if val, ok := memo[n]; ok { return val }`

verification.failureMessage: Compute fib(10)=55 with memoization and print it.
